title: The Thirsty Pigeon

full_text:
A pigeon, tormented by a raging thirst on a scorching summer day, flew frantically over the rooftops in search of water. Every fountain was dry, and the gutters were filled with dust.

Glancing toward the wall of a tavern, the desperate bird saw a large sign depicting a crystal glass brim-full of sparkling, ice-cold water, painted with such exquisite realism by an artist that water droplets seemed to glisten upon its rim.

Deluded by his frantic desire and without stopping to inspect the scene, the pigeon closed his wings and swooped down with reckless speed, intending to plunge into the refreshing vessel.

He slammed headfirst into the hard wooden signboard with a resounding CRACK! The impact broke his wings and shattered his breastbone. Tumbling helpless to the cobblestones below, the dying bird was promptly picked up by a tavern cat, sighing in his final breath: "Alas, my blind haste made an illusion my executioner!"
moral: Blind haste born of desperate desire leads straight into destruction.
